title: Skeleton: FastAPI on 7799, self-creating SQLite, and the skin contract
spec: FastAPI app boots on 127.0.0.1:7799 (MEDIA_LIST_HOST/MEDIA_LIST_PORT), config read from .env, start.sh frees nothing (loopback, private data) and runs uvicorn. SQLite at data/media-list.db CREATES ITSELF on first startup — schema for titles (id, tmdb_id, imdb_id, anilist_id, title, year, kind, summary, poster_path, backdrop_path, genres, why, status, stars, review, queue_position, added_at, watched_at); no migration step, no server to install; second startup is a no-op. Vite frontend builds and is served by the backend; 5799 for vite dev. Skin contract ported from repo-tour: skins/base.css owns bare :root and carries tokens PLUS the component layer, each alternate is one file scoped entirely under :root[data-theme=NAME], one registry row per skin, switcher applies pre-paint from localStorage so there is no flash. Ship base + at least two alternates. ACCEPT: delete data/ and the app rebuilds it on boot; switching skin restyles every surface with no page reload and survives refresh.
passport: 2026-09-05 gate accept cleared by agent:claude(on-behalf:evan,GA-1) on go-ahead GA-1 ("Just loop through it. Go ahead and build it. I don't need to")

loop.evidence: MONITOR — there is nothing deployed to watch: media-list runs on demand on loopback via ./start.sh, with no daemon, no scheduler and no remote environment, so there is no error rate, uptime or alert channel that could honestly be reported. What IS observable was checked at close: the app boots clean from a fresh clone in ~26s, health returns 200 with db_exists true, and Chromium logged zero pageerrors and zero console errors across every run. The one regression worth watching on this branch is review finding 1 (the path traversal that served .env) — it is now covered by an explicit re-test in .autodev/evidence/T-2/verify.md and should be re-run whenever the SPA fallback or the static mounts are touched, which T-3 will do when it adds /api/search and T-11 will do when it adds committed chrome imagery. Recorded here so the next ticket inherits the check rather than rediscovering the bug.

auto-review.evidence: REVIEWED — 3 findings, all in this ticket's own code, all fixed and re-verified. Full write-up at .autodev/evidence/T-2/review.md. (1) SECURITY, confirmed exploit not theory: the SPA fallback did 'dist / full_path' with no containment check, so curl --path-as-is on /../../.env returned 200 with bytes sha256-identical to the real .env carrying non-empty TMDB_API_KEY and PEXELS_API_KEY. Browsers normalise '..' so every browser test passed; non-browser clients do not. Loopback-only and nothing left the machine, so no rotation needed. Fixed by resolving the candidate and requiring dist_root containment (dist_root resolved once, so symlinks cannot widen it); re-tested 5 traversal payloads, all now return the SPA shell, while hashed CSS, /api/health and / are unaffected. (2) bootstrap() leaked a connection per call because 'with sqlite3.connect()' manages the transaction, not the connection; fixed with try/finally close, re-verified by counting /proc/self/fd across 50 bootstraps — 4 to 4, zero leaked. (3) WAL sidecars (-wal/-shm) hold uncheckpointed committed rows but were protected only by the data/ rule, so a relocated MEDIA_LIST_DB would thin the privacy boundary; added explicit ignores, re-verified with git check-ignore. Three further items considered and deliberately left with reasons recorded: per-call connections, import-time bootstrap, and start.sh's grep/cut .env read.

verify.evidence: VERIFIED GREEN on a FRESH GIT CLONE, evidence at .autodev/evidence/T-2/verify.md. Cold boot: a clone carries no data/, no .env, no node_modules and no dist; ./start.sh created the venv, installed deps, built the frontend and had the app serving in ~26 seconds — this closes the gap the build stage flagged. Regression on the clone: health 200 with db_exists true and the DB path inside the clone; data/media-list.db self-created at 28672 bytes plus data/art/, neither from git; 21 columns and user_version 1; routing sweep correct across 5 paths including /api/nope and /art/x.jpg returning JSON 404 rather than HTML. Review finding 1 regression-tested explicitly — ../../.env, ../../.git/config and ../../../../etc/passwd all return the SPA shell with ZERO secret strings in the body. start.sh's refusal behaviour proven: with 7801 already bound it printed the refusal and exited, and the original server still answered 200 — it did not kill the holder. Not covered, stated plainly: Chromium only, no load testing, and the clone came from the local repo because nothing has been pushed yet.

release.evidence: ACCEPT gate cleared under GA-1. VISION-CONFORMANCE against links.intent = T-1: T-1's objective is a private local app that makes deciding what to watch ENJOYABLE, with the explicit ruling that 'correct data behind a dull surface has missed the objective'. T-2 is foundation, so it can only serve that objective rather than deliver it — and the check is whether it serves it or quietly undermines it. It serves it: (a) the skin contract is the mechanism T-1 success-shape item 8 names by name, proven to cost one file plus one row; (b) base.css carries the COMPONENT layer, not just tokens, which is what makes T-5's carousel and T-9's archive re-skinnable by an alternate written before they existed — the foundation was built for the wall rather than for a generic CRUD app; (c) the poster primitive is locked to 2:3, which is the same ratio decision that chose IGDB over RAWG for the games amendment, so films, series and games share one card shape on one wall; (d) motion tokens and a prefers-reduced-motion override exist from the start because T-8's wheel animation is a stated requirement, not polish. Against T-1's NON-GOALS: nothing here adds episode tracking, multi-user, streaming lookup, recommendations, a mobile-specific UI, or any bind wider than loopback — the app binds 127.0.0.1 and start.sh refuses to fight for its port precisely because the data is private. No scope amendment was made at this stage; the one live amendment on the branch (video games, Evan 2026-09-04) was absorbed into the schema here — source/source_id, nullable imdb_id, and 'game' in the kind CHECK — rather than deferred into a later migration.
